Show trials by closed societies should work better but feed the rival's long-run influence narrative — the clinical wire copy of a scripted confession should read as damning to the player who knows it's false, which is exactly the belief-vs-truth feeling the vision doc wants.

key_takeaways: Replace success percentages with pre-commitment OUTCOME LADDERS: 3-5 concrete named world-states (clean success / success-with-evidence / quiet failure / loud failure / catastrophic exposure) with period estimate-language likelihoods (PROBABLE/POSSIBLE/UNLIKELY) derived from inspectable factors — the Invisible Inc/Into the Breach transparency doctrine applied to spycraft, and the antidote to XCOM's 95%-miss betrayal problem.

Failure is content: every loud failure spawns a multi-week U-2-shaped event arc — wire flash, cover-story choice made under uncertainty, enemy-timed evidence reveal, show trial / summit collapse — and being caught lying must cost strictly more than early admission.

Attribution is a three-state machine (UNATTRIBUTED → SUSPECTED → PROVEN) driven by discrete named evidence objects (captured pilot, marked shipment, defected operator), not a meter; only PROVEN works as a crisis pretext, and per Cormac & Aldrich even proven-but-unacknowledged ops escalate less than acknowledged ones — the fiction of deniability is itself an escalation damper, serving the total-war-is-failure thesis.

Three player decisions per op, everything else auto-resolves: AUTHORIZE (type/target/posture with the outcome ladder shown), the AFTERMATH stance (cover story, disavow-or-trade prisoners), and the standing-program budget allocation; no mid-op micro — Terra Invicta's roll-spam is the anti-pattern, Ajax/PBSuccess's authorize-then-watch shape is the model.

Recommended catalog (10): overflight recon, émigré network insertion, coup sponsorship (capstone, wins via manufactured belief à la PBSuccess), clandestine radio, balloon leaflets, cable tap, defector inducement, executive action (taboo-priced, delayed-fuse attribution), party/election funding, deniable arms pipeline — plus defender verbs: CI sweeps and show trials (which can fabricate PROVEN attribution against innocents, the Oatis case).

Espionage product plugs into existing systems: overflights/taps/defectors mechanically shrink the opacity bias on enemy nuclear-program and military estimates already implemented; blown networks get played back to POISON those same estimates (Berlin Tunnel/Philby pattern — the enemy may watch rather than roll up); arms pipelines set the volunteer-formation deniability currency already in the war slice.

All outcomes arrive as period text in three registers — public wire copy, internal numbered-paragraph cables with hedged damage assessments ('ASSESS CAPTURE PROBABLE'), and enemy broadcast/show-trial coverage — never as game-speak toasts; hover-decomposition keeps every consequence explainable.

Key sources: Into the Breach GDC 2019 postmortem (gdcvault.com/play/1025772); Game Developer on Invisible Inc stealth design; NSC 10/2 text (irp.fas.org/eprint/berger.htm); Cormac & Aldrich, 'Grey is the new black', International Affairs 94:3 (academic.oup.com/ia/article/94/3/477); Eisenhower Library & history.state.gov on U-2; Wikipedia/FP on Operation Valuable; CIA Museum & NSA REGAL history on the Berlin Tunnel; militarystrategymagazine.com on PBSUCCESS; rferl.org & coldwarradiomuseum.com on balloon operations; radio.cz & Nieman Reports on the Oatis trial; spotterup.com & theins.org on Stashinsky; CK3 Dev Diary #5 (forum.paradoxplaza.com) on scheme secrecy/breaches.

reports.topic: Espionage layer design synthesis: coupling intelligence to every existing system in the UGS Cold War sim

findings.name: Core stat: one penetration score per (viewer, subject, domain), with exactly four domains
findings.detail: A single per-pair stat cannot express the historically dominant situation: in 1950 the US had decent Korean order-of-battle intel but near-total ignorance of the Soviet nuclear program, while simultaneously reading Soviet political traffic via Venona. Conversely, a free-form per-topic system explodes state and UI. The four existing consumers in the codebase pick the domains for us, 1:1 — NUCLEAR (feeds `believed_deliverable` in crates/ugs-sim/src/deterrence.rs, currently biased only by subject-side `exposure_permille`), MILITARY (replaces hardcoded fuzz widths in the war UI enemy-division/loss estimates), ECONOMIC (sees through `reported_centi` vs `actual_centi` in crates/ugs-sim/src/planning.rs), POLITICAL (narrows the fuzzed Resolve band in crates/ugs-sim/src/crisis.rs and improves crisis-behavior forecasting). HoI4's La Résistance uses a similar per-target 'intel level' split into four categories (civilian/army/navy/air) and it works as a knowledge model; its failure is that intel rarely changes decisions — our four domains each gate a decision the player already makes (launch posture, attack timing, trade/aid stance, crisis brinkmanship), which avoids that trap. Sources: https://hoi4.paradoxwikis.com/Intel, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venona_project.
findings.recommendation: Add `IntelState` resource: `BTreeMap<(CountryTag, CountryTag), DomainPenetration>` where `DomainPenetration { nuclear: u32, military: u32, economic: u32, political: u32 }`, each 0–1000 permille. Keep the existing subject-side `exposure_permille` as 'how loud the program is'; effective nuclear knowledge for a viewer = `clamp(subject.exposure_permille + viewer.penetration.nuclear, 0, 1000)` — a one-line change inside `believed_deliverable`. Iterate the BTreeMap only (determinism). No per-province intel, no named persistent agents in v1.

findings.name: The single asset: one abstract network per (owner, target), built by monthly funding
findings.detail: The espionage.md sketch already leans 'abstract networks + rare named defector/mole events' and that is right: named-operative systems (HoI4 operatives) generate micro without decisions, violating the project's few-meaningful-decisions sensibility. A network is `strength: u32` (0–100) per (owner, target) pair. Funding is a monthly budget command; strength grows deterministically toward a funding-set ceiling, slowed by the target's counterintelligence level and its regime openness (closed/planned societies are harder to penetrate — matching why CIA economic estimates of the USSR were so contested; see https://tnsr.org/2018/02/assessing-soviet-economic-performance-cold-war/). Network strength drives passive monthly penetration accrual per domain, weighted by a player-set collection emphasis (one dropdown: which domain this network prioritizes). All accrual is pure integer arithmetic on `SimClock::new_month` — RNG is reserved exclusively for discrete incidents (exposure, sweeps, defections).
findings.recommendation: Commands: `SetNetworkFunding { target, level: 0..3 }` and `SetCollectionEmphasis { target, domain }` following the existing `SimCommand` pattern in crates/ugs-sim/src/command.rs. Accrual formula lives in a `tuning` module. Penetration decays a few permille monthly when unfunded (sources go stale), so estimates carry an honest 'as of' date.

findings.name: Coupling to deterrence and the economy is nearly free — do these first
findings.detail: The two highest-value couplings are one-liners. (1) Deterrence: `believed_deliverable` currently computes bias = 1000 + opacity * OPACITY_BIAS_PERMILLE / 1000; substituting viewer-adjusted opacity (subtracting penetration.nuclear) makes espionage the direct counter to the bomber-gap overestimate the sim already models — historically it took U-2 and then CORONA imagery to collapse the missile gap from a feared 1000 ICBMs to the actual 4 (https://www.armscontrol.org/act/2011-05/missile-gap-myth-and-its-progeny, https://www.thecrimson.com/article/2011/9/27/gap-missile-cia-soviets/). (2) Economy: rival-visible output = `lerp(reported_centi, actual_centi, penetration.economic / 1000)` — the planned-economy misreporting that is currently invisible becomes exactly as visible as your sources are good, with zero new state. This also makes the AI's threat assessment of the player manipulable in both directions, fulfilling 'what your rival believes matters as much as what is true'.
findings.recommendation: Ship these two couplings in the very first espionage commit, before any ops exist — even a debug-set penetration value immediately makes the existing systems richer. Then wire MILITARY penetration to the war-UI fuzz width (width_permille = BASE_WIDTH * (1000 − pen) / 1000, min floor so estimates are never exact) and POLITICAL to the crisis Resolve band the same way.

findings.name: Deception is the subject-side mirror of penetration — and can be seen through
findings.detail: Extend the existing per-program `deception: bool` (parade deception) into a per-domain deception posture on the subject side: nuclear (parades, decoy airframes — the 1955 Aviation Day flypast that manufactured the bomber gap), economic (inflate `reported_centi` further), military (dummy formations). Deception adds bias to rival estimates only while the viewer's penetration in that domain is below a threshold (e.g. 400 permille); above it, the viewer 'sees through' the deception — fire a teletype event ('SOURCES CONTRADICT OFFICIAL FIGURES') and permanently mark the subject as a known deceiver to that viewer, halving future deception effect and imposing a Resolve penalty in crises between them (a caught liar's threats are discounted). This gives deception real risk, not a free toggle.
findings.recommendation: Replace `SetParadeDeception` with `SetDeceptionPosture { domain, on }`. Store `seen_through: BTreeSet<(viewer, subject, domain)>` — one-way flags, checked before applying deception bias. Keep the threshold and bias magnitudes in `tuning`.

findings.name: Counterintelligence: a passive level plus a sweep event that produces spy trials
findings.detail: Defender-side: `counterintel_level: 0..3` per country (a command, with monthly budget cost). Effects: (a) subtracts from all foreign networks' accrual against you; (b) on `new_month`, one deterministic sweep roll from `rng.fork(b"ci-sweep")` per (defender, strongest-network owner) pair, success probability scaling with counterintel level and network strength (big networks are loud). A successful sweep degrades the network sharply and fires a choice event for the DEFENDER through the existing event engine — the spy-trial event, three options mirroring the historical repertoire: (1) PUBLIC SHOW TRIAL: +domestic legitimacy/ideology points, +global tension, propaganda win — the Powers trial model (https://adst.org/2013/01/the-show-trial-of-u-2-pilot-francis-gary-powers/); (2) QUIET EXPULSION: no tension, banks a 'held agent' counter enabling a future Abel-Powers-style swap event that reduces tension (https://www.history.com/articles/u2-spy-incident); (3) TURN THE AGENT (requires counterintel 2+): network owner's penetration of you becomes a deception channel for N months — their estimates of you get worse while they believe they are getting better. Option 3 is the deep cut; it can defer to v1.5 if needed.
findings.recommendation: Sweep rolls iterate defenders in BTreeMap order; at most one trial event per defender per month to avoid event spam. Trial outcomes route through the existing `ResolveEvent` command path, so replays are safe by construction.

findings.name: Mole hunts: the Angleton tradeoff as a single command
findings.detail: An active `OrderMoleHunt` command (distinct from passive counterintel): for 6 months, all foreign penetration of you decays rapidly AND your own collection accrual against everyone is halved — internal suspicion paralyzes the service, which is precisely what Golitsyn-driven mole hunting did to CIA and to French intelligence (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatoliy_Golitsyn, https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/08850607.2025.2574292). Domestic cost too (purge unrest for closed regimes, scandal for open ones). This is the cleanest possible expression of the historical cost structure: one decision, real tradeoff, explainable numbers.
findings.recommendation: V1.5, not v1 — it needs the defector system (below) to supply the mole *leads* that motivate the hunt. Implement as a timed status on the country, decremented on `new_month`.

findings.name: Defectors: rare events delivering a truth snapshot plus a penetration spike
findings.detail: Defectors were the Cold War's highest-density intel deliveries — Gouzenko alone reframed Western understanding of Soviet operations (http://intellit.muskingum.edu/russia_folder/russiasovdef_folder/russiasovdefa-j.html). Model: monthly roll from `rng.fork(b"defector")` weighted by the subject's domestic conditions (purges, low legitimacy, recent crisis climb-downs increase odds; this couples espionage to the future ideology pillar for free). Delivery: one-time +150–250 permille in one or two domains, plus an 'as-of-date snapshot' estimate card showing near-truth values frozen at the defection date — which then age, teaching the player that intelligence is perishable. A defector event can also carry a mole lead (enables/strengthens a mole hunt) or, rarely, be a plant seeding false confidence (the Golitsyn ambiguity) — flag plants only in the sim, never the UI.
findings.recommendation: Ship a minimal version in v1 (spike + snapshot card only, 2–3 flavor texts in the clinical wire voice); mole leads and plants in v1.5. Defectors are cheap given the event engine already exists and they are the system's best narrative delivery vehicle.

findings.name: Sabotage vs collection: acting through a network spends and risks it — the OSO/OPC tension as one resource
findings.detail: CIA's collection arm (OSO) and covert-action arm (OPC) literally collided in the field, 'intelligence fratricide,' until forced to merge in 1952 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_Policy_Coordination). Codify it: sabotage ops are commands that (a) require network strength above a floor, (b) consume strength on execution, (c) roll blown/clean from `rng.fork(b"op-resolve")` with blow-chance scaling with target counterintel and current tension band. V1 sabotage targets the nuclear hooks that already exist: knock a `FacilityKind` level down for N months, or apply a `speed_mod_permille` malus (the unused stolen-design modifier becomes the mirror op: a tech-theft op granting the ATTACKER a speed bonus — the Fuchs/Rosenberg channel, which historically accelerated the Soviet bomb). Clean op: quiet effect, small penetration loss. Blown op: full network loss in that country, tension spike sized by tension band, deniability hit, and a crisis-pretext event.
findings.recommendation: Commands: `LaunchOperation { target, op: Sabotage(FacilityKind) | StealDesigns }`. Resolve during `TickSet::Politics` on the tick after command application. Gate op availability on network strength so the tradeoff is felt: a network strong enough to sabotage is a network delivering good estimates you will lose.

findings.name: Blown ops are the crisis system's pretext factory, and deniability is the damping stat
findings.detail: The U-2 shoot-down killed the Paris summit — a collection failure that manufactured a superpower crisis (https://www.history.com/articles/u2-spy-incident). The crisis system needs pretexts; the espionage system generates them: every blown op emits a wire event tagged as a usable pretext for the victim (open a crisis at an elevated starting rung, or bank it). Deniability: per-country 0–100 stat. A blown op spends 10–25 depending on op audacity; at low deniability the tension cost of the NEXT blown op multiplies (nobody believes your denials — the sketch's 'U-2 problem'), and you suffer a Resolve penalty in crises where your op is the pretext. Regenerates ~2/month; a `Scapegoat` command (burn the agency head) restores a chunk at domestic-legitimacy cost. This makes deniability a real currency, per the vision, with four integers of state.
findings.recommendation: V1 ships blown-op → tension + pretext event + a simple deniability counter with the multiplier. Scapegoat command and Resolve coupling in v1.5. Tension-band gating: at Brink, blow-chance and tension cost both scale up, so covert action self-limits exactly when the player is tempted to overreach.

findings.name: Decrypts and overflights are v2 — each is a full mechanic with its own dilemma, and each has a natural unlock date
findings.detail: Decrypts (Venona model): a standing cryptanalysis investment per pair yielding slow political/nuclear penetration — with the signature dilemma that ACTING visibly on decrypt-sourced intel (arrests, trials) risks burning the source entirely; the US sat on Venona for years for exactly this reason, and it was blown by a mole (Weisband) anyway (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venona_project). That source-protection choice deserves its own events and should not be crammed into v1. Overflights (U-2 model): mid-1950s tech unlock, per-mission command, large nuclear/military penetration spike on success, shoot-down chance from target air defense and alert level — a shoot-down producing a captured-pilot spy trial FOR THE OTHER SIDE, a ready-made pretext, and a big deniability spend. Satellites (late-50s+) then obsolete overflight risk, historically ending the missile-gap era of wrongness (https://www.cia.gov/legacy/museum/exhibit/corona-americas-first-imaging-satellite-program/) — the tech ladder gives the espionage layer its era arc for free.
findings.recommendation: Design both now (one paragraph each in the doc, hooks reserved: an `IntelSource` enum on accrual so per-source attribution exists from day one), implement after v1 proves the penetration loop. Overflights before decrypts — they reuse the crisis/trial machinery v1 builds.

findings.name: UI: a dossier Intelligence panel where every estimate explains its own provenance
findings.detail: The genre's chronic failure is intel the player cannot act on or explain (HoI4 decryption 'I do not even bother' — https://steamcommunity.com/app/394360/discussions/0/601907675997958983; Stellaris/MoO endgame irrelevance). The project rule 'every number the player sees should be explainable' is the fix, applied to uncertainty itself. Per rival, four domain cards (reusing the existing estimate-card component): a period-voice coverage grade — NEGLIGIBLE / LIMITED / PARTIAL / EXTENSIVE, mapped to penetration quartiles — the current estimate with its band, an AS OF date (last meaningful accrual or defector snapshot), and a provenance line in the clinical NIE register ('DERIVED FROM: OFFICIAL STATEMENTS (contested), SOURCE REPORTING'). Real NIEs carried exactly this confidence language. Add a monthly INTELLIGENCE SUMMARY wire item on `new_month` when any rival's grade changed — the teletype engine already does this style. Critically: the panel shows YOUR OWN exposure too (each domain: how penetrated rivals likely are of you, itself an estimate) — that is what motivates counterintel spending and closes the loop.
findings.recommendation: One new panel (`UGS_PANEL=intel` dev shortcut), built entirely from the estimate-card primitives in ugs-app. Never print raw penetration permille; only grades and bands. The war-UI and deterrence displays keep their existing look — their widths just become live values from the intel stat instead of hardcoded fuzz.

findings.name: Determinism and scheduling contract for the whole layer
findings.detail: Everything above reduces to: integer permille state in BTreeMaps keyed by CountryTag pairs; passive accrual and decay computed on `SimClock::new_month` (never tick-modulo); discrete incidents (sweeps, defections, op resolution) drawn from labeled forked streams — `b"ci-sweep"`, `b"op-resolve"`, `b"defector"`, `b"crypt-burn"` reserved — iterated in sorted key order; every player decision a `SimCommand` variant applied in `TickSet::Commands` and thus in the replay-safe log; event choices through the existing `ResolveEvent` path. Estimate DISPLAY fuzz (the 2-sig-fig rounding) stays presentation-side and non-random per existing practice; the sim stores true values plus per-viewer penetration, and the app derives bands — so saves stay small and no believed-value ever needs serializing.
findings.recommendation: Run the sweep/op/defector systems in `TickSet::Politics` (after Commands, before Military) so a sabotage landed this month affects this month's production. Add headless tests: (1) two runs same seed bit-identical with espionage active, (2) penetration monotonically narrows the deterrence bias, (3) month-rollover and 1952 leap-year cadence, per project convention.

findings.name: V1 scope cut
findings.detail: V1 (ships first, roughly in commit order): IntelState 4-domain penetration + wiring to all four existing consumers (deterrence bias, economic lerp, war-UI fuzz width, crisis Resolve band); abstract networks with funding/emphasis commands and deterministic monthly accrual/decay; counterintel level + monthly sweep; spy-trial choice event (trial/expel options); nuclear sabotage + StealDesigns ops with blown-op → tension + pretext event + simple deniability counter; minimal defector event (spike + snapshot); the Intelligence panel. V1.5: turn-the-agent option, mole hunts + mole leads, scapegoat command, deniability–Resolve coupling, deception see-through events, prisoner-swap events. V2: overflights (with the mid-50s tech gate and shoot-down crisis loop), cryptanalysis/decrypts with source-burning, defector plants, satellites. Explicitly OUT of this pillar: election ops, coups, propaganda — those belong to the influence pillar and should consume this layer's networks/deniability when built, not duplicate them.
findings.recommendation: The v1 line is drawn so that every existing system visibly changes behavior (the four couplings) before any new content is authored, and so the only new UI is one panel. Estimated state added to the sim: ~6 integers per country pair plus ~4 per country — trivially serializable, trivially deterministic.

key_takeaways: One stat per (viewer, subject, DOMAIN) with exactly four domains — nuclear, military, economic, political — because each domain maps 1:1 onto an existing consumer in the codebase (deterrence.rs opacity bias, war-UI fuzz widths, planning.rs reported-vs-actual, crisis.rs Resolve band). Per-pair-only is too coarse for the historical texture; more than four domains is state without decisions.

The two best couplings are one-liners and should land first: viewer penetration shrinks the deterrence opacity bias (the bomber-gap/missile-gap collapse, historically ended by overflights and satellites), and rival-visible planned-economy output becomes lerp(reported, actual, penetration/1000).

One abstract network per (owner, target) is the sole asset; sabotage and tech theft SPEND and RISK the network that also collects — the OSO/OPC 'intelligence fratricide' tradeoff as a single resource. Blown ops feed the crisis system's pretext demand and the tension meter, damped by a deniability counter (the U-2 problem: each blown op makes the next denial worth less).

Counterintel is a passive level plus a monthly sweep whose success fires a spy-trial CHOICE event — show trial (+domestic, +tension), quiet expulsion (banks a swap), or turn-the-agent (feeds deception) — reusing the replay-safe event/command machinery wholesale.

Determinism is easy if incidents and accrual are separated: passive accrual/decay is pure integer math on new_month; only discrete incidents (sweeps, op resolution, defectors) touch RNG, via labeled forks (b"ci-sweep", b"op-resolve", b"defector") over sorted BTreeMap keys; all decisions are SimCommand variants.

UI rule: never show raw permille — show period-voice coverage grades (NEGLIGIBLE/LIMITED/PARTIAL/EXTENSIVE), an AS-OF date, and an NIE-style provenance line on every estimate card, plus your own counter-exposure; this is what saves the system from the genre's ignorable-espionage failure mode (HoI4 decryption, Stellaris endgame).

Cut line: v1 = stat + networks + counterintel/spy trials + nuclear sabotage + pretext/tension/deniability + minimal defectors + one panel; v1.5 = mole hunts, turned agents, swaps, scapegoats; v2 = overflights (mid-50s tech, shoot-down crisis loop) and Venona-style decrypts with source-burning; election ops/coups belong to the influence pillar and should later consume this layer, not duplicate it.
